scope: Shared privileged archive import and its existing deployment tests/documentation only. No web or capability-coverage edits. The old round6 audit report remains unchanged.
implementation: Added deploy/archive.py; safe_fs.extract_tar now uses its sequential decoder and clears completed TarInfo cache entries. All source/tool/edge consumers keep using the same extract_tar entry point.

A guarded TarInfo._proc_member runs before PAX/GNU payload processing for each physical header. Bounds: 64 KiB per extension, 64 KiB UTF8 effective/global PAX state using surrogateescape, 64 MiB aggregate extension payload, 16 nested extensions, three physical headers per logical member limit (450000 by default). Effective PAX-overridden file sizes are checked before payload reads/seeks. Unsupported sparse formats fail closed before sparse-map processing.

Raw/compressed input has a 4 GiB cap and sequential decoded bytes have an explicit total covering data plus bounded metadata/header/padding allowances, including skipped members. Individual reader requests are capped at 1 MiB. gzip/bz2 use bounded-output buffered readers; XZ uses max_length output chunks and a 128 MiB decoder memory limit. Empty XZ outputs are never accumulated.

Preserved ordinary PAX/GNU long filenames and links, global metadata, raw/gzip/bzip2/XZ and explicitly named legacy .lzma archives, concatenated compressed streams and XZ padding. Existing filesystem safety and immutable release checks remain active.

Extended ArchiveTests in existing tests/deploy/test_deployment.py; no new test filename or deploymentPairs mapping was needed. scripts/select-tests.mjs already routes deploy/*.py to the deployment domain.

beforeAfter.conclusion: The original 246-byte gzip with 65536-byte PAX metadata was accepted under scaled 1-byte budgets; it is now rejected with budget. A declared 536870913-byte PAX header previously caused a 536871424-byte parser read request; final code rejects it after a largest observed 10240-byte request. No actual large allocation or OOM was attempted.
